questionBank.questionText: According to the CAP theorem, when a distributed data store experiences a network partition (P), which trade-off is unavoidable?

options.label: A
options.text: Choosing between linearizable Consistency (C) and 100% Availability (A)

options.label: B
options.text: Choosing between Durability and Horizontal Sharding

options.label: C
options.text: Guaranteeing both strict linearizability and zero-latency writes on all nodes

options.label: D
options.text: Disabling TLS encryption to preserve TCP throughput

questionBank.explanation: During a network partition (P), nodes that cannot communicate must either reject/delay requests to preserve linearizable Consistency (CP) or serve potentially stale data to remain Available (AP).
questionBank.subject: Distributed Systems

questionBank.questionText: Which defense-in-depth controls directly mitigate Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) when rendering untrusted page text in a browser dashboard? (Select all that apply)

options.label: A
options.text: Context-aware HTML output encoding and safe DOM APIs (textContent)

options.label: B
options.text: Strict Content Security Policy (CSP) disallowing unsafe-inline scripts

options.label: C
options.text: Passing raw extracted HTML directly into innerHTML and eval()

options.label: D
options.text: Sanitizing and stripping executable script/iframe tags prior to storage

questionBank.explanation: Safe DOM sinks (textContent), strict CSP headers, and input sanitization prevent untrusted data from executing as code.

questionBank.questionText: True or False: In Raft consensus, a follower node can unilaterally commit log entries without a majority quorum if its local clock is synchronized via NTP.
questionBank.explanation: Raft safety requires a leader elected by a majority quorum and replication across a majority of cluster nodes before committing any log entry.

questionBank.questionText: When designing retry logic for transient RPC timeouts in distributed microservices, which strategy prevents synchronized retry storms across clients?

options.label: A
options.text: Exponential backoff combined with randomized jitter and bounded retry limits

options.label: B
options.text: Unbounded zero-delay tight-loop retries on every client thread

options.label: C
options.text: Fixed 100ms synchronized cron retries across all worker nodes

questionBank.explanation: Instructor Explanation: Exponential backoff with randomized jitter spreads out client retries and prevents cascading thundering-herd overload. (Note: Sourced from instructor lecture notes; not yet verified by an official grading key.)
questionBank.subject: Distributed Systems
